question: What is the main difference between a smart bed and a traditional hospital bed?

options.A: Smart beds use motorized mechanisms and digital sensors.
options.B: Smart beds require manual cranking for all position changes.
options.C: Traditional beds feature automated patient weight monitoring.
options.D: Traditional beds have built-in electronic health records.

explanation: Smart beds rely on automated motors and integrated sensors to carry out functions that traditionally required manual effort. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which hospital unit benefits the most from the advanced monitoring features of smart beds?
explanation: Units caring for critically ill patients rely heavily on smart beds for continuous monitoring and rapid positioning adjustments. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which component of a smart bed lifts and tilts the mattress platform?
explanation: Actuators provide the mechanical power needed to adjust the height and angle of different bed sections. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h2)

question: How do exit-detection systems usually alert nurses that a patient is getting out of bed?

options.A: By using load cells or beams to trigger an alarm
options.B: By automatically locking all the wheels on the frame
options.C: By inflating the mattress side bolsters rapidly
options.D: By sending a text message to the hospital kitchen

explanation: Load cells and infrared sensors detect changes in weight distribution or movement, instantly alerting staff to potential falls. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which patient is the best candidate for an automated bed exit alarm?

options.A: Experiencing mild dehydration on oral fluids
options.B: Recovering from a stable wrist fracture
options.C: At high risk for falls due to confusion
options.D: Scheduled for a minor skin biopsy

explanation: Patients who are confused or unsteady are prime candidates for exit alarms to prevent unassisted, dangerous attempts to get up. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why are bariatric smart beds particularly helpful for nursing staff?

options.A: They reduce physical strain during patient repositioning.
options.B: They allow patients to walk unassisted much faster.
options.C: They eliminate the need for any nursing documentation.
options.D: They completely cure chronic underlying obesity.

explanation: Automated functions on heavy-duty beds spare nurses from heavy manual lifting and reduce workplace musculoskeletal injuries. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of continuous lateral rotation therapy in a smart bed?

options.A: To speed up the digestion of tube feedings
options.B: To make it easier to change bed linens completely
options.C: To redistribute pressure and prevent tissue breakdown
options.D: To measure the exact height of the patient daily

explanation: Continuous lateral rotation gently turns the patient to relieve prolonged pressure on bony prominences, protecting skin integrity. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h4)

question: How do smart bed scales improve accuracy when weighing vulnerable patients?

options.A: They calculate weight using only the angle of the head board.
options.B: They weigh the patient directly on the mattress without transfers.
options.C: They estimate weight based strictly on the patient's height.
options.D: They require the nurse to lift the patient off the bed first.

explanation: Weighing integrated into the bed frame allows precise measurements without disturbing critically ill or unstable patients. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h4)

question: What must a nurse check before turning on the automated turning features of a smart bed?

options.A: That tubing and cords have enough slack
options.B: That visitor chairs are pushed far away
options.C: That the patient has eaten a full meal
options.D: That the primary room windows are open

explanation: Ensuring lines like IV tubing or urinary catheters have slack prevents accidental pulling or dislodgement during bed movement. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is regular testing of the bed backup battery important in clinical practice?

options.A: To calibrate the built-in nurse call system volume
options.B: To ensure positioning controls work during power failures
options.C: To prevent the mattress from becoming too warm
options.D: To stop the bed from moving around the room

explanation: Emergency backup power guarantees that essential adjustments and alarms remain functional when electricity fails. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is the first step a nurse should take if a smart bed control panel stops working?

options.B: Check the power source and connection plugs
options.C: Transfer the patient to a stretcher immediately

explanation: Simple power checks resolve many basic electronic failures before involving specialized technical repair teams. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h6)

question: Why is special care required when cleaning the electronic components of a smart bed?

options.A: To prevent liquid from damaging internal sensors and wiring
options.B: To stop the cleaning chemicals from smelling too strong
options.C: To make the outer frame dry within five minutes
options.D: To ensure the bed changes color when washed properly

explanation: Moisture seeping into electronic seals can ruin actuators, sensors, and control systems, rendering the smart bed useless. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h6)
